questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The possibility of doing outdoor activities, being closer to nature, an active student environment, and the population should be able to speak English at an ok level.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy - all the information was available on the NMBU website, even though it could be a bit tricky to find the right web pages in the beginning.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had received all the information necessary prior to arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Many options: dorms from 4-16 people or student apartments. Easy to get an overview of the different options and apply for housing through the website
www.sias.unialltid.no
.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: At my dorm (Palisaden) the kitchen was fully equipped with pots and pans and cutlery. The building is quite new (2012-14), and the kitchen is very big and clean and has ovens, microwave oven, freezers, and induction stoves.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Do it! And I would recommend to chose a dorm with as many people as possible - I lived with 15 other students, and it was never too much. We made a lot of social activities together, and I liked that there was always someone home for a chat or walk.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't remember it very well, but we got a lot of help - there was a presentation and walk-through of the process, and the staff was available for guidance afterwards.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: see above

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't get all the courses I wanted - NMBU is very strict when it comes to prerequisites, and there is also some courses that are only possible to apply for if you are registered in a master's or bachelor's programme (not exchange student). But even though you don't get the courses you originally wanted, you should definitely apply for exchange at NMBU anyways!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you have any questions don't hesitate to call or write an email to the university!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't get exactly the courses I wanted.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses I followed were at a bit lower level than I am used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style varies a lot depending on the course, but I was a bit unlucky: a lot of the teaching was solely one-way communication from the professor. I missed that the professor actively engaged the students by asking questions or making discussion groups, etc. I didn't have a lot of group work either.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MVI310 Macronutrients, Their Structure and Functionality
MVI393 Chemical Food Safety
FMI312 Environmental Exposures and Human Health
MTH300 E-learning Course: Planning and Scientific Writing of a Master's Thesis in Natural Sciences

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I was particularly happy with the MTH300 E-learning Course: Planning and Scientific Writing of a Master's Thesis in Natural Sciences. I got a lot of tools and useful information for my future master's thesis.
I can also recommend MVI310 Macronutrients, Their Structure and Functionality if you like food chemistry. But expect group work with people from other countries and cultures, which might create some challenges. However, I think meeting and working with people from other cultures is an important part of exchange!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Membership in the gym and in some student organisations, concerts at the Students' house (Samfunnet).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Local transportation - I went to Oslo 1-2 times per week, and a oneway ticket to Oslo costs approx. 47 DKK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There were an endless number of student organisations! Many different sports clubs, choirs, dancing associations and music associations. Also many political organisations, outdoor groups, gaming groups, botanics,climbing, etc. 
Every second year NMBU students arrange a festival called UKA, which lasts throughout October. There are a lot of concerts and other events such as revy / sketch show.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Be part of an organisation! Doesn't matter which one - it is just a really good and easy way of getting to know people who share common interests with you. 
I was part of two associations, which ended up being my primary social groups: an association dancing nordic folk dance (Leikarringen Frøy), and an association playing folk music (Flatlusa). Bring your instrument and your best dance moves! ;)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Become a member of the outdoor life association - they arrange many trips in the weekends. Generally, the different student associations have a lot of activities in the weekends, so don't be afraid to get bored, it's not going to happen.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Luckily, Norwegians understand Danish quite well, so it is not too difficult to become friends with the local people. The culture is also somewhat similar to the Danish culture, but Norwegians can seem a bit "cold" or difficult to get to know. Don't let that scare you! But don't expect them to seek your company - you have to do the hard work in the beginning :)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: see above

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That many Norwegians enjoy outdoor life!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be part of a student assocaition!
Learn to bake your own ryebread! Norwegian rugbrød is not really rugbrød...
If you drink alcohol you should bring some from Denmark - it is really expensive in Norway.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Doing things I would never do in Denmark and just saying yes to everything!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That I could not say exactly what I wanted to say or be as fun as I use to be in Danish, because I had to be conscious about my word choice when speaking to Norwegians (because they don't understand everything you say if you don't speak slow and substitute some words).

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
